'''Concha Maria Gómez''' is an American mathematician. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Diablo Valley College]]. Gómez is known for being one of the co-founders of the women's organization ''The Noetherian Ring''<ref name="The Noetherian Ring – Women in the Department of Mathematics at UC Berkeley">{{cite web | title=History – The Noetherian Ring | website=The Noetherian Ring – Women in the Department of Mathematics at UC Berkeley | url=https://nring.math.berkeley.edu/history/ | access-date=2022-11-30}}</ref> at the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California Berkeley]] in 1991 while attending as a doctoral student. She is an advocate for diversity in the STEM fields and worked for the Wisconsin Emerging Scholars program of the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], whose goal was to promote retention of minority students in STEM.

== Early life and education ==
Gómez was born to Patricia M. Difanis Gómez and Nicolas Humberto Gómez.<ref name="phd dissertation"/> She attended [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] for two years before dropping out due to lack of funds and support. She moved from Madison to [[San Francisco]] at the age of 20 and worked odd jobs before taking classes for fun at a community college. Gómez eventually transferred to [[University of California, Berkeley]] and earned a B.A. and Ph.D. in mathematics in 2000.<ref name="science 20050513"/>

Her dissertation was titled "Definability in p-adic [[power series]] rings."<ref name="phd dissertation" /> [[Leo Harrington]] was her doctoral advisor. [[Jack Silver]] and [[Deborah A. Nolan]] served on her dissertation committee. Gómez cites the support of [[Jenny Harrison]] and [[Donald Sarason]] for encouraging her to form relationships with mathematicians outside of UC Berkeley.<ref name="phd dissertation" />  Gómez is known for being one of the co-founders of the women's organization ''The Noetherian Ring'' at the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California Berkeley]] in 1991 while attending as a doctoral student.<ref name="noetherian ring site"/><ref name="science 20050513" />

== Career ==
Gómez was an assistant professor of mathematics at [[Middlebury College]]. In the fall of 2004, she began working at [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in a non-tenure track position to teach math and direct the Wisconsin Emerging Scholars (WES) program whose goal was to promote retention of minority students in STEM.<ref name="science 20050513" /> In 2006, Gómez cited [[Same-sex marriage in Wisconsin|Wisconsin's passing a constitutional amendment banning same-sex marriage]] as a motivation to seek academic employment elsewhere.<ref name="badger herald 20061206"/> She is a professor of mathematics at [[Diablo Valley College]] where she is also fostering a support network of [[Latinx]] faculty and students. She is an advocate for diversity in the STEM fields.<ref name="mashable 20180906"/>

Gomez is included in a deck of playing cards featuring notable women mathematicians published by the [[Association of Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematicians of EvenQuads Deck 1 |url=https://awm-math.org/publications/playing-cards/deck1/#gomez |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=awm-math.org}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Concha Gómez was diagnosed with [[multiple sclerosis]] as a doctoral student.<ref name="science 20050513" />
